_meta.purpose: Shared owner-action scenario -> keyword-terms data, unifying the two independent implementations that previously drifted (spec §1 drift #5): web-admin restaurantOwnerActionRegistry.ts (frontend inference) and backend restaurant_sections.py _OWNER_ACTION_KEYWORDS (backend topic-gate + fallback inference).
_meta.merge_policy: Per-scenario term set = union(frontend_terms, backend_terms), EXCEPT where a term maps to a DIFFERENT scenario across the two sources AND adding it to the frontend's scenario would come earlier than the backend's current scenario in the backend's iteration order (see excludedConflicts below) -- those are excluded from the union to guarantee zero behavior regression in the backend fallback loop (first-match-wins over scenarios in tuple order).
_meta.revenueGrowth: revenue_growth exists only in the frontend registry. Backend handles it via separate compound-phrase logic (_infer_owner_action_scenario_from_message top-of-function literal phrases + _is_broad_revenue_growth_question), not via this flat keyword-tuple mechanism. Registered here (backendKeywordGate=false) for completeness / future convergence, but NOT loaded into the backend's runtime _OWNER_ACTION_KEYWORDS tuple -- adding it there would newly open the topic gate for terms that previously didn't engage the owner-action feature at all, which is a materially bigger change than simple term-widening and out of A1's zero-regression scope.

excludedConflicts.reason: staff_training appears LATER than staffing_schedule in the backend's iteration order. Backend already resolves a message containing only '服务员' to staff_training today. Adding it to staffing_schedule (earlier in order) would silently steal that match. Excluded from staffing_schedule's term list to preserve current behavior; still present under staff_training (already there in both sources).

single_item_push appears LATER than package in the backend's iteration order. Backend already resolves a message containing only '加购' to single_item_push today. Adding it to package (earlier in order) would silently steal that match. Excluded from package's term list; still present under single_item_push (already there in both sources).

otherKnownAmbiguities.note: operations_dispatch is earlier in backend order and already contains this term, so it already wins today; adding to staffing_schedule too is safe (dead weight for that specific term, doesn't change any outcome, but documented for human review since it is a genuine semantic ambiguity between the two systems).
external_event_response is earlier and already contains this term, so it already wins today; safe to also list under package.
operations_dispatch is earlier and already contains this term, so it already wins today; safe to also list under staffing_schedule.

otherKnownAmbiguities.frontend: ambiguous within frontend itself (present under BOTH inventory_reorder and cost_margin in restaurantOwnerActionRegistry.ts)
otherKnownAmbiguities.backend: was absent from both scenarios pre-merge (dead keyword, no match)
otherKnownAmbiguities.note: Added to inventory_reorder only (earlier in backend order than cost_margin), mirroring how the frontend's own array-order resolution would already prefer inventory_reorder. Pure coverage gain -- backend previously had zero match for this term.
